newsitem.title: PERU: Peru says Doe Run decides to buy 100 pct La Oroya.
newsitem.headline: Peru says Doe Run decides to buy 100 pct La Oroya.

text.p: Peruvian state miner Centromin said Friday the United States' Doe Run Co had agreed to buy its La Oroya metallurgic complex, following an earlier decision by Mexico's Industrias Penoles SA de CV to withdraw its offer.

Doe Run agreed to pay $126.5 million to increase the company's capital with an initial offer to buy 51 percent of the complex and had further agreed to buy the remaining state shares for "about $120 million," Centromin said in a statement.
Centromin said that while Doe Run had decided to buy all the state's shares, the deal would "fully respect" the workers' priority right to buy up to a 10 percent stake in the complex.

Industry analysts, however, have said the workers' preferential rights would not likely affect the sale because traditionally the state miner's employees opted to buy only a very small percentage of shares in the privatization programs.
Doe Run, the largest integrated lead producer in the United States and a subsidiary of Renco Group of New York, was runner- up to Penoles in an April 18 auction for rights to La Oroya.
Penoles surprised the mining world by abandoning plans to acquire a 60 percent stake in the complex, claiming Centromin burdened the asset with additional liabilities after the sale.

La Oroya lies in the country's central Andes 12,300 feet (3,700 meters) above sea level and 120 miles (190 km) east of Lima. The complex of refineries and smelters processes 22 metals and their byproducts.
Centromin's asset sales are part of its continued piecemeal privatization, which is set to continue with the auction of mines, hydroelectric plants and polymetallic minerals.
